q: The Chernoff bound provides exponential concentration for sums of independent random variables. For a sum S = X₁+…+Xₙ with E[S] = μ, it states P(S ≥ (1+δ)μ) ≤:
exp: The Chernoff bound: P(S ≥ (1+δ)μ) ≤ (e^δ/(1+δ)^{1+δ})^μ ≤ e^{−μδ²/3} for δ ∈ (0,1). This exponential decay (vs. polynomial for Chebyshev) makes Chernoff bounds much tighter for algorithms analysis.
